name: Jean-Charles Naouri
current_role: President of Euris SAS (holding company); former chairman-CEO of Groupe Casino until March 2024
profile: French financier who left the civil service in 1987 to found investment holding Euris, then bought Rallye (1991) and used a layered holding structure to control retailer Groupe Casino from 1992. CEO of Casino until a 2024 debt restructuring handed control to Daniel Kretinsky's consortium and wiped out most of his stake.
interesting_fact: As chief of staff to finance minister Pierre Bérégovoy (1982-86), he is credited with France's 1984-86 financial-market reforms, including creation of the MATIF futures market and MONEP options market.
deep_cut_fact: He won first prize in Latin and Greek at the Concours général aged 14, got his baccalauréat at 15, and placed first in the 1967 École normale supérieure entrance exam; he is honorary president of the Institut de l'ENS.
notes: Lost control of Casino in March 2024 (https://esmmagazine.com/retail/french-retailer-casino-changes-leadership-team-as-boss-naouris-era-ends-262309). French Wikipedia reports a Jan 2026 Paris court conviction for private corruption and spreading false information, so check this before any outreach. Very private, with no personal public channels. Forbes listing is from 2015 and he is likely no longer a billionaire.

name: Laurent Burelle
current_role: Chairman of the Board, OPmobility SE (formerly Plastic Omnium); CEO of family holding Burelle SA
profile: Son of Plastic Omnium founder Pierre Burelle, he joined the family group in the mid-1970s, ran it as CEO from 2001 to 2019 and refocused it on automotive exterior systems and fuel tanks. Now non-executive chairman of OPmobility (renamed 2024), where daughter Félicie Burelle became CEO after Laurent Favre left in Nov 2025. He led French business lobby Afep from 2017 to 2023.
interesting_fact: Under his chairmanship Plastic Omnium was renamed OPmobility in 2024 and has invested in hydrogen mobility (tanks, fuel-cell systems) and electrification, which is relevant to an energy podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He started at the group's Langres plant around age 25 after initially planning to work for Alfa Laval, and at 28 moved to Spain to run the Valencia plant, becoming head of the Spanish subsidiary in 1980. He trained as a chemical engineer at ETH Zurich and MIT.
notes: Governance change Nov 2025: Félicie Burelle took over as CEO (https://www.opmobility.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/evolution-in-the-governance-of-opmobility-se-20251107-en.pdf). Best route is via OPmobility corporate communications. Wiki sources disagree on the exact chairmanship start date (2020 vs 2021).
